description: Finalized ROTOM prompt templates for direct inference, the orchestrator, workers, and aggregator, including shared task and state information.
scope: Finalized agents used in live development and final ROTOM evaluation. Earlier preliminary and exploratory offline prompts are outside this package.

assembly.instruction_stripped: Trim leading and trailing whitespace after filling the selected role instruction; preserve all internal whitespace. Interpolate each template once; do not interpret braces within inserted game text or JSON as new placeholders.

optional_header_lines.condition: round_index is not null, including zero

sections.name: calculations
legal_actions

rendering.mapping: Empty mapping: (none). Otherwise join with newlines: - {key}: {value}, sorting outer keys. Values use Python str(), preserving nested dictionary insertion order, single quotes, True, False, None, and tuple notation.
rendering.history: Empty transcript: (no prior rounds). Otherwise join entry lines with newlines. Each entry begins with - and a space, then available fields in order: [round N], speaker:, action={Python dictionary}, message="text", separated by spaces. A raw entry is rendered only if no formatted fields are available.
rendering.identity: game_family is the lowercased family name. Header role is the original player slot supplied by the server. Functional role for checklist selection uses the state declaration first, otherwise player_1/player_2 map to alice/bob for Bargaining and seller/buyer for Negotiation and Persuasion.
rendering.configuration: Copy only exposed configuration fields; never fill missing private information. The current state remains the server-visible state.
rendering.calculations: Deterministic facts computed from the visible observation before any model call; the same values are supplied to every role. Fully constructed examples retain their calculated values.

textual_task_description.source: The literal GLEE game.prompt string, converted to text when non-null.
textual_task_description.insertion: Under ## SERVER DESCRIPTION, unchanged, in every request for that decision.
textual_task_description.content: Observed game rules, role, payoff parameters, horizon, current situation and server action instructions.
textual_task_description.scope: The server description varies with the observation. The following are complete observed descriptions, not universal server generator templates.

representative_descriptions.name: bargaining_decision
representative_descriptions.text:
You are Bob, negotiating with Alice over how to divide $1,000,000.
The game lasts up to 12 rounds.
Each round, 20.0% inflation erodes your share (its value is multiplied by 0.8 per round).
When responding to an offer you can also leave the bargaining by choosing 'walkaway' — the money is not divided, and you and Alice both get $0.
If no agreement is reached after 12 rounds, both players get $0.

Round 1 of 12.

Alice proposed: Alice=$901,000, Bob=$99,000
Respond with JSON: {"decision": "accept"}, {"decision": "reject"}, or {"decision": "walkaway"} (leave — the money is not divided, both get $0)

representative_descriptions.name: bargaining_offer
representative_descriptions.text:
You are Alice, negotiating with Bob over how to divide $10,000.
There is no limit on the number of rounds: the game continues as long as offers keep being rejected.
When responding to an offer you can also leave the bargaining by choosing 'walkaway' — the money is not divided, and you and Bob both get $0.
If you never reach an agreement, both players get $0.

Round 1.

It's your turn to propose a split.
Respond with JSON: {"alice_gain": amount, "bob_gain": amount}
The two amounts must sum to 10000.

representative_descriptions.name: negotiation_decision
representative_descriptions.text:
You are a buyer. The product is worth at most $150.00 to you.
You want to buy it for as low a price as possible.
You can walk away at any time by choosing 'WalkAway' (you and the seller both get $0 profit).
This is a single-round negotiation: there is one offer, and no counteroffer is possible.
If no agreement after 1 rounds, both get $0.

Round 1 of 1.

The seller offered $105.50.

Your options:
  {"decision": "AcceptOffer"} - accept the price
  {"decision": "RejectOffer"} - reject; no counteroffer is possible, so this ends the negotiation (both get $0)
  {"decision": "WalkAway"} - walk away (both get $0)

representative_descriptions.name: negotiation_offer
representative_descriptions.text:
You are a seller. Your product is worth at least $10,000.00 to you.
You want to sell it for as high a price as possible.
You can walk away at any time by choosing 'WalkAway' (you and the buyer both get $0 profit).
There is no limit on the number of rounds: the negotiation continues as long as offers keep being rejected.
If no agreement is ever reached, both get $0.

Round 1.

It's your turn to make a price offer.
Respond with JSON: {"product_price": amount}

representative_descriptions.name: persuasion_buyer_decision_binary
representative_descriptions.text:
You are a buyer. Each round a seller offers you a product at $10,000.00.
There is a 50% chance each product is high quality (and 50% low quality).
You value high-quality products at $40,000.00 and low-quality products at $0.00.
You only learn a product's actual quality if you buy it. If you pass, the quality stays hidden.
Your goal is to maximize your total earnings (value - price for purchases).

The game lasts 20 rounds.
Round 1 of 20.

The seller says: "no"
Do you want to buy? Respond with JSON: {"decision": "yes"} or {"decision": "no"}

representative_descriptions.name: persuasion_buyer_decision_text
representative_descriptions.text:
You are a buyer. Each round a seller offers you a product at $10,000.00.
There is a 33% chance each product is high quality (and 67% low quality).
You value high-quality products at $30,000.00 and low-quality products at $0.00.
You only learn a product's actual quality if you buy it. If you pass, the quality stays hidden.
Your goal is to maximize your total earnings (value - price for purchases).

The game lasts 20 rounds.
Round 1 of 20.

The seller says: "I recommend buying this product."
Do you want to buy? Respond with JSON: {"decision": "yes"} or {"decision": "no"}

representative_descriptions.name: persuasion_seller_message
representative_descriptions.text:
You are a seller. Each round you have a product to sell at a fixed price of $100.00.
There is a 50% chance each product is high quality (and 50% low quality).
You know the actual quality of each product before the buyer decides.
The buyer values high-quality products at $120.00 and low-quality products at $0.00.
Your goal is to maximize your total earnings by selling as many products as possible.
You earn $100.00 for each sale.

The game lasts 20 rounds.
Round 1 of 20.

This round's product is **low quality**.
Send a message to the buyer. Respond with JSON: {"message": "your message"}

representative_descriptions.name: persuasion_seller_recommendation
representative_descriptions.text:
You are a seller. Each round you have a product to sell at a fixed price of $10,000.00.
There is a 50% chance each product is high quality (and 50% low quality).
You know the actual quality of each product before the buyer decides.
Your goal is to maximize your total earnings by selling as many products as possible.
You earn $10,000.00 for each sale.

The game lasts 20 rounds.
Round 1 of 20.

This round's product is **high quality**.
Do you recommend this product? Respond with JSON: {"decision": "yes"} or {"decision": "no"}

representative_descriptions.name: negotiation_counteroffer_history
representative_descriptions.text:
You are a seller. Your product is worth at least $10,000.00 to you.
You want to sell it for as high a price as possible.
You can walk away at any time by choosing 'WalkAway' (you and the buyer both get $0 profit).
There is no limit on the number of rounds: the negotiation continues as long as offers keep being rejected.
If no agreement is ever reached, both get $0.

Round 2.

Previous rounds:
  Round 1: seller offered $18,000.00 → RejectOffer (counter: $12,000.00)

The buyer offered $12,000.00.

Your options:
  {"decision": "AcceptOffer"} - accept the price
  {"decision": "RejectOffer", "product_price": your_counter} - reject and counter
  {"decision": "WalkAway"} - walk away (both get $0)

shared_decision_instruction:
Make a strategically informed decision. Use the full game state, the public history, the other party's observed behaviour and signals, the deterministic calculations, and the remaining horizon, to the extent each of those is available to you. The deterministic calculations are supporting facts, not a complete strategy. Where they are relevant, weigh the immediate payoff, the future consequences of the action, and what the action reveals to the other party.

Your goal is to win this game and maximize our competition performance.
For this decision, choose the legal action that maximizes OUR OWN expected
game utility/payoff and chance of a favorable outcome. When monetary payoff
applies, prioritize our own monetary utility. Consider the current state,
observed opponent behavior, remaining horizon, and future consequences.

The strategic action is primary. Send text only when required by the game or
when it is strategically useful.

checklists.bargaining:
Consider:
- the payoff consequences of delay
- what you know about the opponent's patience
- the offer and concession history so far
- the remaining horizon and the risk of no deal
- what your next action reveals about you
checklists.negotiation:
Consider:
- your own payoff constraints
- your uncertainty about the opponent's valuation
- the information revealed by their offers and messages
- how much bargaining opportunity remains
- the risk of no deal versus extracting more surplus
checklists.persuasion_seller:
Consider:
- the current product's economics
- the buyer's beliefs and the trust you have observed
- the information revealed by your past messages and their outcomes
- long-term reputation versus an immediate sale
- the consistency of your signalling across rounds
checklists.persuasion_buyer:
Consider:
- the prior economics: the stated probability of high quality, the two values,
  and the price
- what this round's seller signal does and does not tell you
- the history of past signals and their outcomes, and what it suggests about
  how this seller uses signals
- what you learned about quality from rounds you actually bought in
- how many rounds remain
- the trade-off between acting on your current beliefs and learning more about
  how this seller signals
checklists.persuasion_unresolved_role:
Consider:
- the prior economics: the stated probability of high quality, the values, and
  the price
- what this round's signal does and does not establish
- what past signals and their outcomes reveal about how signals are being used
- what the observed history has settled versus what remains uncertain
- how many rounds remain
- the consistency of signalling across rounds

orchestrator.instruction_template:
3 assistants will each independently propose a complete action for this
turn. They will all see exactly the information you just read. They work in
parallel, cannot talk to each other or to you, and each will return a full
legal action. You will then choose the final action yourself.

Write exactly 3 short analytical questions, derived from THIS state, that are
worth examining before committing to a move. Each must be answerable from the
information above, be one sentence, and be materially different from the other
two. Two different game states should generally produce different
questions.

Do not name roles, do not name models, and do not give any assistant
information the others lack.

Return a JSON object: {"tasks": ["...", "...", "..."]}

worker.instruction_template:
You are one of three assistants advising on this turn. You work alone and
cannot see the other two.

The decision-maker wants this perspective examined:
{task}

Use that perspective to inform your reasoning, then solve the WHOLE decision.
Do not return a partial analysis, and do not answer only the perspective:
return the single complete legal action you would take this turn.


{worker_action_output_format}

aggregator.instruction_template:
## CANDIDATE ACTIONS
{candidate_header}

{candidate_blocks}

Decide this turn yourself. The candidates are input, not a vote.

- Evaluate each candidate against the game state above on its own merits.
- Agreement between candidates is not evidence. Do not choose an action because
  more than one assistant proposed it.
- Check that the action you choose is legal here and consistent with the state,
  the history, and the remaining horizon.
- Choose the single action that best advances our own payoff.
- If none of them is the best available move, construct a different legal
  action instead.

Return exactly ONE complete legal action.

{final_action_output_format}

dynamic_construction.worker_tasks: The orchestrator returns tasks: three nonblank one-sentence questions. Trim outer whitespace, retain order, assign one question to each worker. No fixed personas. Each worker sees the complete shared information and independently proposes a complete action.
dynamic_construction.emergency_task_template: [emergency-decomposition] Independent analysis {i} of 3. Analyse this decision on its own terms and state what action you would take and why.
dynamic_construction.emergency_condition: If delegation fails or does not yield exactly three nonblank questions, use the emergency task for i=1,2,3 without an extra delegation call.
dynamic_construction.candidate_header_template: {n} of 3 assistants proposed a complete action for this turn. They worked independently from exactly the information you have. The candidates are unlabelled and their order carries no meaning.
dynamic_construction.candidate_format: Use Python str(action) for each action dictionary. Strip rationale whitespace, truncate to 600 characters, and replace empty or missing rationale with (none given). Separate blocks by two newlines. Positions start at 1.
dynamic_construction.no_candidate_text: None of the 3 assistants returned a usable action. Decide without them.
dynamic_construction.candidate_order: Retain usable candidates in worker-brief order, then cyclically rotate. Let key be game_id + : + Python str(round_index), hash UTF-8 key with SHA-256, interpret its first eight bytes as an unsigned big-endian integer and take modulo n. Output candidate indices (i + offset) modulo n for i=0..n-1. With n<=1 keep input order.
dynamic_construction.candidate_visibility: The aggregator sees actions and rationales only: no worker identifiers, assigned perspectives, providers or model names.
dynamic_construction.output_format: Derive the action fields, numeric bounds, choices and conditional fields from the legal-action description and documented game contract. Direct and aggregator share the final-action output format; workers use candidate_action. Exact text variants and field templates are provided below.

final_action.first_line: Return a single JSON object with these keys:
final_action.unconstrained_action_line: - "action": an object holding the move, using exactly the field names the legal-action description above calls for
final_action.optional_total_line: The values of {numeric_fields_python_list} must sum to exactly {total}.
final_action.optional_message_line: - "message": text to send to the other party, at most {max_message_len} characters; use "" to send nothing
final_action.rationale_line: - "rationale": one or two sentences of your reasoning (kept internal)

worker.first_line: Return a single JSON object with EXACTLY these two keys:
worker.optional_total_line: The values of {numeric_fields_python_list} must sum to exactly {total}.
worker.rationale_line: - "rationale": one or two sentences of your reasoning (optional)
worker.last_line: Name the action key "candidate_action". Do not call it "action", and do not nest it inside another object.

field_description_templates.unconstrained: the field names the legal-action description above calls for
field_description_templates.conditional_numeric: "{name}": number - include it ONLY with {allowed_choices} (there it is {requirement}); omit the key entirely otherwise
field_description_templates.optional_numeric: "{name}": number, optional - omit the key when it does not apply

rendering_rules: Join field descriptions with ; and a space, in order: numeric fields, optional numeric fields, required text fields, discrete choice field.
Use -inf and +inf for missing lower and upper bounds when either bound is specified.
Join quoted choice values with space, vertical bar, space. For conditional numeric fields use space, or, space; use REQUIRED if required_for is nonempty, otherwise optional.
Include the total line only when total is non-null and more than one numeric field exists.
Include the separate message line only when add-on text is allowed. In seller text mode message is a required action field instead.
Join output-format lines with one newline.

game_contracts.fields: alice_gain, bob_gain; sum to the advertised total or money_to_divide
decision: AcceptOffer | RejectOffer | WalkAway; product_price only with RejectOffer
game_contracts.counteroffer_rule: Counteroffer required unless state establishes the final round. Unknown horizon does not establish the final round.

game_contracts.fields: message: required text inside the action
